desc:
A tree has n nodes numbered 0..n-1 and is rooted at node 0. The array parent gives the parent of each node, with parent[0] = -1. Node v carries the letter s[v].

Look at paths in the tree, in any direction (a path may go up and then down). A path is valid if no two neighbouring nodes on it carry the same letter. Return the largest number of nodes of a valid path. A single node is a valid path.

parent = [-1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], s = "abacbe"

3 - 1 - 5 uses letters c, b, e   (valid, 3 nodes)
3 - 1 - 4 is invalid (b, b);  3 - 1 - 0 - 2 is invalid (a, a)   -> 3
constraints: parent[0] = -1, and every other entry is a node number in 0..n-1 such that the whole array forms a tree rooted at 0 (a parent can have a larger number than its child)
s consists of lowercase letters a-z
hints: Without the letter rule this is the tree diameter in nodes. Think about how the diameter DP changes when a chain cannot continue into a neighbour with the same letter.
For each node v compute the longest valid chain going down from v. A child c may extend the chain of v only when s[c] != s[v].

At each node keep the two longest chains among its children with a different letter. The best path through v has top1 + top2 + 1 nodes; the chain passed up to the parent is top1 + 1. Process nodes in reverse BFS order to avoid recursion.
editorial: This is the tree diameter DP with a filter. Let chain[v] be the maximum number of nodes of a valid path that starts at v and only goes down. Then chain[v] = 1 + max(chain[c]) over children c with s[c] != s[v] (just 1 if there is no such child).

A valid path that has v as its highest node uses at most two child branches. Both branches must start at children with a letter different from s[v]; they may have equal letters with each other, because the two children are not neighbours on the path. So the best path with top node v has 1 + best1 + best2 nodes, where best1 and best2 are the two largest chain[c] among allowed children (missing branches count as 0). The answer is the maximum of this over all nodes.

Build children lists, order nodes by BFS from the root, and process the order backwards so that children are done before parents. Each node updates its parent's two best values in O(1). The total time is O(n), space O(n).
